title: 'There are no bad tunes' at the Grand Terrace
summary: Armstrong turns a disliked tune into a hit at Chicago's Grand Terrace.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Well, they have a few things you'd ask for that we didn't have. We had really everything in the album. Russ, we had it from Red Allen or we had it from Pops. You had to read a big book. Yeah, he had a hell of a book. Russ had music, no. You didn't play many heads at all? No, we didn't. We had played most arrangements. I'll tell you one time, yeah, we were in Chicago at the Grand Terrace for two weeks. Fox had the job. And I remember, Joe Clayton's buddy. And you remember? My name is the shame. They had an arguing in the band. Somebody said, but I don't like this tune. I don't like that tune. And I remember at the rehearsal, Lewis said, Pops said, man, let me tell you, there's no bad tunes. All tunes are good. What do you mean, Pops? It's the way you play them. There's no bad tunes, I tell you. The guy said, yeah, no bad tunes. He said, there's no bad, and I noticed one thing, everything he made was a hit. And he's right, there's no bad tune. So, me and Mr. Shen had just come out, that she called them. And during the animation, the band was off to stand. And just Louie, Pop, and Paul Barberin, and Pop Foster, and Lee Blair, stayed on the stand. And Pops, Joe Russell, played with me and Mr. Shen. Just by himself. And Louie played such a beautiful horn. I never heard, he's always playing arrangements, you know. Now he's at live. Pops started blowing, and the people started, what? They went crazy. And Pops took about eight chorus of Lumi and the band. And they said, man, now we had to keep that number in for two weeks because they thought it was in the act. They thought it was in the act, you know. Hey, that number of the Pops, they ain't playing the band no mine. They want to hear Louie. And Louie said, you see what I tell you? There's no bad tune. Now we were convinced, you know. Now that we, I knew it all. Come on. Lord, Louie shook him. Louie's in good form. Oh, man. That was the time when Joe Louie was champion, and he was there with his wife that night. He just played. That place was packed. And every night, Louie had to do Louie. That Mr. Shen business.
Oh, that was funny. He could make the people like anything, did he?

I'm telling you, I never heard of him sound bad through the ears. Anything he played, it was in that song. Oh, Lord, Lord. Well, he was right. That's the way you played. Hey, cats, I don't like this number. I don't know why. I don't like it. Oh, come on.
